`tools/parity-matrix.py` from 2026-10-25 on** (JUnit `@Tag("CUS-04")` in `src/test`, Playwright
title prefix `[CUS-04]` in `e2e/tests`, merged with the last `target/*-reports` and
`e2e/test-results/results.json`; run it after `./mvnw -B -ntp verify` and `e2e/run.sh`;
`--check` is the CI guard to add). The "Planned tests" and "Notes" columns stay hand-maintained
(the generator never touches them; the frozen `docs/parity-plan.md` of the original plan was
dropped with the lighter process of 2026-10-24 — this file is the single table). Statuses:
**planned** · **in progress** · **green** · **ready-for-owner** · **blocked (Q-xx)**. An ID is
green only when at least one real test tagged with it passed in the last run (never a
placeholder); the coverage block lists the evidence per ID. NFR-05, NFR-06 (deploy part) and
NFR-07 reach **ready-for-owner at most**: they ship the script, workflow or runbook and become
green only with a dated rehearsal record (who, when, result) under `docs/rehearsals/`.
MIG-01…03 stay **blocked (Q-55)**.

Every ID of chapter 09 appears exactly once (78 IDs: PUB 11, TRK 4, API 3, CUS 7, ADM 12,
EML 9, MIG 3, NFR 7, ENH 22; CUS-07, ADM-11 and ADM-12 added on the owner's request of 2026-10-25). Owners are those of `docs/plan.md` §4.2; layers are those of
chapter 10 §6 (unit · integration · contract · E2E · quality · migration · rehearsal).

Cross-cutting for every EML-ID: every integration test asserts recipient, subject, Reply-To
and the key content (09 EML acceptance); Reply-To rule (ADR 0015 default): customer-facing
e-mails carry Reply-To = `ls.business.office-email`, office notices carry Reply-To = the
customer's address where one exists (EML-06, EML-08), else none. Outside production no
e-mail reaches a real recipient: the staging-guard integration test of the NFR-04 row (the
context fails to start without a mail catcher or an allow-list; a non-allow-listed recipient
is dropped and logged) carries `@Tag("NFR-04")` plus every EML-ID, so it counts for each of
them; a failing SES fake never rolls back the business action;
the outbox retries with backoff and a dead state.
